units.function: HTTP authorization regression suite for plugin installation/lifecycle/configuration, manifest-scoped routes, local-folder configuration, tool execution, generic worker bridges, manual jobs and Agent-JWT plugin tool access.
units.dependencyDirection: Authenticated board/Agent request actors enter pluginRoutes; route policy consults actor Company/admin scope, plugin manifest/registry, secret service and relational Agent/run/project ownership before invoking lifecycle, worker bridge, job scheduler or tool dispatcher.
units.keyDataModels: Board/Agent actor and Company IDs; plugin ID/key/manifest/capability/API route; package/version/lifecycle; secret_ref/version/target binding; runContext Agent/run/Company/project; bridge key/params/actorContext; tool identity; job; structured bridge error.
units.lifecycle: Discover/install/upgrade/configure/enable/disable/uninstall plugins; save scoped secret references; dispatch declared HTTP routes; validate local folders; execute a plugin tool under run context; call data/action bridges; trigger jobs; expose tools to authenticated Agents.
units.testAssessment: All 36 tests pass outside the network-restricted sandbox. The suite has valuable tenant checks: instance-admin lifecycle gates, cross-Company secret rejection before binding, manifest route declarations, undeclared folder rejection, DB validation of runContext references, Company scope override and Agent JWT Company boundaries. It does not establish a safe human delegation model: opaque bridge params retain spoofed reviewer IDs, and board actions are allowed with userId null. It also lacks exact actor-Agent/run equality, Agent permission/tool/data/cost policy, exhaustive route auth/capability modes, package signature/provenance, CSRF/idempotency, lifecycle impact approval/rollback and stable redacted worker errors.
units.designRationale: Centralize plugin-facing HTTP access behind authenticated Paperclip routes so extension code receives scoped context and cannot directly choose a different Company or secret binding.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs an extension gateway that is narrow, auditable and responsibility-aware across managed cloud and local enterprise, not a generic bridge that trusts plugin-defined params after only replacing companyId.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT the broad getData/performAction bridge and unrestricted Agent tool execution as the production contract. ADAPT its instance-admin lifecycle checks, secret-reference tenant validation, declared routes, and server-side runContext lookup. Define typed per-capability commands generated from versioned schemas; bind authenticated Principal directly and remove all actor/reviewer IDs from plugin-controlled params; reject missing human identity for human actions. Verify Agent actor equals run Agent and exact Work/Contract/permission/data snapshots; require tool capability, budget and approval. Use opaque local handles, signed packages, staged upgrade/rollback, CSRF/idempotency and stable redacted error codes. No global action may receive all tenant state implicitly.
units.responsibilityConflict: The route supplies authenticated actorContext but also forwards spoofable identity-like plugin params, while downstream host services accept bare actorUserId for interactions/approvals. A board actor with null userId may also invoke actions. Thus the gateway does not guarantee that the human recorded in the responsibility chain actually initiated or authorized the action.

2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 0/36 passed solely due Supertest TCP listen EPERM
units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: plugin lifecycle/config requires instance admin; secret refs are tenant-validated before binding; manifest route/folder declarations constrain surfaces; non-admin/global and cross-Company actions are rejected; runContext Agent/run/project tenant relationships are checked; authenticated actorContext overrides companyId. CRITICAL identity gap: spoofed reviewer IDs remain in opaque params and missing board user identity is accepted, so downstream privileged host calls can still fabricate human attribution. HIGH Agent confused-deputy gap: no test proves authenticated Agent equals runContext Agent within the same Company. HIGH permission gap: Agent JWT tool access is not bound here to tool capability, data grant, approval or budget. HIGH supply-chain gap: install/upgrade lacks signature/hash/allowlist/impact approval tests. HIGH information disclosure: raw worker/database error text is returned with UNKNOWN. MEDIUM global-action risk: instance admins can invoke Company-less actions against a plugin architecture whose worker may hold multi-tenant state. MEDIUM web-security gap: CSRF, idempotency and rate limits are absent.
